MINOR: `validType` defaults to `return true` for any unrecognized `want` spec: a typo in `eventContractTypes` (e.g. `"interger"`) silently disables that check, failing open on the exact drift the map exists to prevent.

Type/enum metadata is split into a new `eventContractTypes` map parallel to the existing `contractShapes` inside `pfcore.go`; two Go sources of truth for one contract invite intra-file drift — consider one canonical structure.

New `for field, want := range types` in `Validate` iterates a map, so multi-error output ordering is nondeterministic — same diagnostics-stability class as the prior `eventContractFields` finding, newly introduced by this hunk.

`TestEventingTypeAndEnumParity` exercises only 4 of the declared fields; the `object`/`array`/`boolean` branches (`payload`, `extensions`, `channels`, `filter`, `enabled`, `attempts`, `throttle_window`) are unexercised, so type parity for those shapes remains unproven in Go.

Numeric check accepts only `int`/`float64`: a valid integer carried as `int64` (hand-built Go payloads) or `json.Number` (decoder with `UseNumber`) is falsely rejected as invalid — brittle for future callers.
Non-string `event_version` now yields two errors for one defect (`"must be string"` from the envelope block and `"invalid type"` from the types loop), duplicating diagnostics.
NIT: Test resolves the contract name via label-string equality (`if label == "bad transport"`); a label edit silently changes the contract under test — a small `label → name` table would be self-describing.
`"seq string"` case name says "string" while asserting integer enforcement; pairing label with expected error message would make failures self-explanatory.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly resolves both prior MAJORs: non-string `event_version` is now rejected, and Go type/enum validation plus a parity test were added — AC-1 evidence for this delta is sound and tests are fail-able.
Remaining risk is fail-open validation semantics (unknown type spec passes, split metadata map) and partial branch coverage of `validType`, which leaves part of the shape-parity obligation unproven.
No blockers; ship after hardening the default case and extending the parity test to object/array/boolean fields.
